text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like NVDA on 2026-09-18, the median realised return over the next 5 sessions was 0.86%. The distribution is wide and slightly right-skewed, with a standard deviation of 3.8%, meaning the path over one trading week historically ranged from -7.34% to 10.25%. This is a description of a conditional historical distribution, not a forecast of what NVDA will do next.

[state]
The engine retrieved these 50 analogs because the current state combines several distinctive features. NVDA is sitting -6.03% from its 52-week high (z-score 0.564) after a 60-session return of 11.82% (z-score 0.39). Its own 20-session realised volatility is elevated at 45.77% (z-score 0.824), while the benchmark 20-session volatility is compressed at 9.16% (z-score -0.574). WTI crude has moved 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124), the most extreme macro feature in the vector. Dollar volume is running below its regime average, with a 20-session dollar-volume z-score of -0.62. The event calendar is empty, with 0 scheduled events in the next 5 sessions (z-score -0.496) and 45 calendar days until the next earnings release. These features collectively pull in names from Technology (9 analogs), Energy (4 analogs), and various sector ETFs, spanning sessions from 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-08.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of 0.65% and a median of 0.86%. The spread is substantial: the 10th percentile sits at -4.04%, the 25th at -2.03%, the 75th at 3.07%, and the 90th at 4.68%. Returns finished above zero in 56% of the episodes and below zero in 44%. The left tail is populated by specific failures. The closest analog is NVDA itself on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2999), which went on to lose -5.9% over the next 5 sessions, suffering a max adverse excursion of -7.44% while only reaching 0.2% on the upside. Another NVDA episode on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.4317) did the opposite, returning 9.66%. The bad tail also includes XLK on 2026-08-13 (distance 0.4178), which returned -4.02% with a max adverse excursion of -4.38%. On the positive side, LLY on 2026-08-13 (distance 0.4066) returned 3.08%, and MU on 2024-01-16 (distance 0.4111) returned 3.45%. The conformal interval, scaled to hit an 80% coverage target, runs from -4.12% to 5.83%, a total width of 9.95%.

[tails]
A position can end the week near flat but still be un-holdable through the middle. Across the 50 analogs, the median maximum adverse excursion during the 5 sessions was -2.01%. The 25th percentile of adverse excursion was -3.77%, and the 10th percentile was -4.38%. In 8 of the 50 episodes, the path breached a 5% drawdown at some point before the horizon closed. None of the 50 episodes breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown threshold. The median maximum favourable excursion was 2.55%, with the 75th percentile at 4.39% and the 90th at 6.71%. The historical reward-to-risk ratio, measured as the ratio of favourable to adverse excursions, was 1.27.

[stress]
The stress scenarios show how this baseline shifts under specific regimes. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario is the most severe: across 48 analogs, the median 5-session return drops to -5.4%, a delta of -6.26 percentage points versus the baseline. The 10th percentile falls to -14.14%, and 58.3% of those episodes breached a 10% drawdown. However, central-bank backstops arrived inside that window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare (50 analogs) produces a median of -3.02% (delta -3.88%), with a 10th percentile of -6.18%, though it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019 that flatters late-window analogs. The 2022 inflation/rate bear (50 analogs) yields a median of -2.42% (delta -3.28%) and a 10th percentile of -8.44%; treat it as a regime description rather than 50 independent events, because the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples a nine-month window repeatedly. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind (36 analogs) shows a median of -2.11% (delta -2.97%) and a 10th percentile of -8.61%, but the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2025-04 tariff shock (26 analogs) gives a median of -2.7% (delta -3.56%), with policy reversals inside the window making the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2023-03 regional bank stress (36 analogs) actually improves the median to 1.51% (delta +0.65%), but the analog set is dominated by a handful of sessions due to the very short window. A +2 sigma VIX spike (50 analogs) shifts the median to -0.18% (delta -1.04%), but VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. A +1.5 sigma policy-rate re-pricing (50 analogs) moves the median to -0.39% (delta -1.25%), using DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies whose transmission to a single name depends on duration and balance sheet features not present here. The liquidity air pocket scenario (50 analogs) leaves the median nearly unchanged at 0.83% (delta -0.03%), but gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not on a 7x24 venue; for the tokenised wrapper NVDAG_USDT, the reference market is closed for 81.4% of the week and 55.21% of the wrapper's realised hourly movement happened in those closed hours, so the gap risk is not hypothetical. Earnings day (50 analogs) lifts the median to 1.61% (delta +0.75%), but earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. FOMC day (50 analogs) drops the median to 0.07% (delta -0.79%), but only 92 decision days exist in the calendar, so the analog set is small and highly overlapping. Crypto contagion (50 analogs) yields a median of 0.8% (delta -0.06%), but the BTC feature is a market-wide proxy and any name-level linkage to crypto flows is not identified. China ADR de-rating (50 analogs) gives a median of -0.06% (delta -0.92%), but delisting and audit-access risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space. No scenarios were skipped.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." At matched coverage, the analog method is -7.6% less sharp than a simple same-name unconditional band. The directional hit rate is 50.1%. The dataset spans 2513 sessions across 71 symbols from 2016-09-20 to 2026-09-18, built on daily adjusted closes from api.stockanalysis.com.

If you trade this view through the verified tokenised wrapper NVDAG_USDT on Gate.io spot v4, its status is "measured" and it carries its own risks. It is classified as a "fair tracker" with a return correlation of 0.8971 and a tracking error of 114 bp/day against NVDA raw session closes over 55 overlapping sessions. The premium band over the underlying's last raw close of 222.27 ranges from -0.44% (10th percentile) to 0.65% (90th percentile), with a price deviation of 2.09%. The resting spread is 7.94 bps. As noted in the wrapper caveat, a fair tracker is not the underlying—at 114 bp/day of tracking error the wrapper carries its own idiosyncratic risk, and the premium band means your exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on.

Crucially, the reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week (136.67 hours), yet 55.21% of the wrapper's realised hourly price movement happens during those closed hours. Over 4 observed weekend blocks, the median weekend block return was 0.569%, the 10th percentile was -1.8803%, and the standard deviation was 1.7703%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.7295%, and 0% of those 4 weekends breached a 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut. They are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying. With only 4 distinct weekend starts observed, the pooled figures overstate the number of independent observations.
